body.heading: Words that sound the same at the end
paragraphs: Some words rhyme: cat and hat, sun and fun, bear and chair. Rhyming words end with the same sound.
Say a word out loud. Can your adult find a word that rhymes? Then swap. Silly made-up rhymes count too, and they are often the funniest.

body.heading: The rhyming chain game
paragraphs: Start with one word, like “cake.” Take turns adding a rhyming word: cake, bake, lake, snake, shake.
Keep going until nobody can think of another one. Then start a new chain with a different word. There is no winner; the chain belongs to everyone.

body.heading: Make a two-line poem
paragraphs: Pick two rhyming words and put one at the end of each line. “I saw a cat / wearing a hat” is a whole poem already.
Say your poem out loud together. Poems are allowed to be very short and very silly.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: play with words that rhyme and build a tiny poem together.
